_comment: NativeIntempt.ts is excluded because it is a type-only TurboModule spec — an
interface plus a TurboModuleRegistry.getEnforcing call. There is no behaviour
to mutate, and its contents are checked by check-corpus.mjs against the
contract instead.
break is 95, set AFTER measuring rather than aspirationally. The suite scored
77.67 on its first run at 99% statement coverage, which is the whole argument
for mutation testing: every surviving mutant was on a line the tests already
executed.
THE THREE EQUIVALENT MUTANTS ARE IGNORED AT THE LINE, NOT EXCLUDED HERE. Each
carries a `// Stryker disable next-line` directive with its reason written
beside the code, so the justification cannot drift away from the line it
justifies the way a file-level exclusion or a line number in this file does. A
previous version of this comment cited src/index.ts:66 and src/errors.ts:77 and
both had already moved. The three, located by CODE:
src/errors.ts, IntemptError's constructor `Object.setPrototypeOf` call
— only load-bearing when transpiled to ES5. This build targets
esnext, where instanceof works without it.
src/index.ts, encodeValue()'s `value !== null` operand
— typeof null === 'object', so the mutant calls
encodeProperties(null), which returns null. Identical output by
a different route.
src/index.ts, numberVariation()'s `typeof value === 'number'` operand
— Number.isFinite does not coerce, so it is already true only
for values of type number. Not removable: it carries no type
predicate, so tsc needs the typeof check to narrow unknown.
Ignoring a mutant removes it from the denominator, so the ceiling is 100 rather
than the ~99 the previous comment claimed — but only for these three, and only
with the reason next to the code.
concurrency is 2 deliberately. Stryker counts a TIMED-OUT mutant as KILLED, so
a machine competing with its own test runs inflates the score and the inflation
is indistinguishable from progress. The timeout count is not stable across
machines — the same commit timed out 4 mutants on CI and 2 locally — so read the
`# timeout` column and subtract it before believing a score that sits near the
gate.
